entries.appliesTo: covered online services conducting business in South Carolina that are reasonably likely to be accessed by minors and meet revenue or data-volume thresholds

dutySources.takedown-process: § 39-80-60(A) — 'Covered online services shall establish mechanisms for parents, minors, and schools to report harm to minors on covered online services'
dutySources.documentation: § 39-80-60(D) — 'required to describe in its terms and conditions, in a clear, conspicuous, and easy-to-understand manner, how the systems are used to provide information to minors'
dutySources.impact-assessment: § 39-80-70(A) — 'Annually, on or before July first, the covered online service must issue a public report prepared by an independent third-party auditor'

sources.admOptOut: § 39-80-30(B) — 'must provide to a user the option to opt out of personalized recommendation systems, except for optimizations based on the user's expressed preferences'
sources.minorsFocus: § 39-80-10(8) — '"Minor" means a consumer who is less than eighteen years of age.'
sources.enforcer: § 39-80-80(A) — 'The Attorney General shall enforce the provisions contained in this chapter.'

flags: bill title describes a social media company act, but the enacted text ('Amend Title to Conform') adds Chapter 80, Title 39, 'Age-Appropriate Code Design' binding 'covered online services' — coded from the enacted text per rule 1

AI nexus is definitional/algorithmic: § 39-80-10(9) 'An online service may include any service, product, or feature that is based in part or in whole on artificial intelligence'; personalized recommendation systems (§ 39-80-10(12)) and profiling (§ 39-80-10(15)) are defined as automated processing
duty of 'reasonable care in the use of a minor's personal data and the design and operation of the covered online service' to prevent enumerated harms (§ 39-80-20(A)) fits no listed duty key

required user tools to disable covered design features, limit time and purchases, restrict visibility/contact/indexing/location (§ 39-80-30(A)), with highest-protection defaults for known minors (§ 39-80-30(C), § 39-80-40(G)) — no matching duty key

data minimization and purpose limitation, targeted-advertising ban to minors, default limits on precise geolocation collection, and notification quiet-hour tools (§ 39-80-40(A)-(E)) — privacy duties with no matching duty/param keys
profiling of a known minor prohibited unless necessary to the requested service (§ 39-80-40(F)) — no profiling-prohibition param in the privacy-data vocabulary
parental tools required and on by default for known minors, incl. account-settings control, purchase restrictions, time-of-day limits, with notice to the minor (§ 39-80-50) — no matching duty key

ads directed to minors for prohibited products banned (§ 39-80-60(B)); dark patterns prohibited and made 'an unlawful trade practice under Section 39-5-20 of the South Carolina Unfair Trade Practices Act' (§ 39-80-60(C)) — cross-referenced enforcement not imported per rule 4

the annual § 39-80-70 report must be 'submitted to the Attorney General who shall post it in a prominent place on his internet website' and include 'description of algorithms used by the covered online service'; age verification is contemplated ('age verification or estimation methods used') but not mandated — no age-assurance duty coded

exposure: no fixed fine stated; 'liable for treble the financial damages incurred as a result of a violation' (§ 39-80-80(B)) and officers/employees 'may be held personally liable for wilful and wanton violations' (§ 39-80-80(C))
